video.title: Overlooked Businesses You Can Start for Almost Nothing

summary: Chris Koerner interviews franchise adviser and entrepreneur Alex Smerzneck about franchising as a way to own a business with a proven playbook. Alex recommends private insurance adjusting, home sale preparation, and custom window boxes, then discusses artificial turf and cleaning franchises. They also cover franchise financing, evaluating disclosure documents, and how multi-unit ownership can scale. Alex promotes Franzy, his franchise-matching platform, which creates a promotional conflict when he discusses franchise opportunities.

ideas.name: Private insurance adjusting franchise
ideas.one_liner: A franchise that helps policyholders negotiate larger insurance claims in return for a percentage of the claim.
ideas.business_model: Franchise; the adjuster takes a percentage of the total claim, subject to minimums.
ideas.customer: People or businesses with fire, water, hail, or other insured property damage.
ideas.problem: Policyholders may not know how to negotiate a claim or believe the insurer's initial offer is too low.
ideas.offer: Assess damage and negotiate with the insurance company on the policyholder's behalf.

pricing.model: Percentage of the total claim, with minimums; exact standard rate not stated.
pricing.notes: Alex gives 10% as an example, not a stated universal rate.

acquisition_channels.details: The franchisor provides leads and lead-generation tools; specific channels are not stated.

ideas.delivery: A trained and, where required, licensed franchisee assesses and negotiates claims. The franchisor provides training, branding, tools, leads, and established relationships.
unit_economics_claims: Alex claims average revenue of $2.6 million per operator and startup costs of $5,000 to $10,000 when financed.
He claims gross margins of 70% to 90% and net margins of 25% to 45%.
He says the referenced franchise fee is $43,000 and discusses an example of a $2,000 claim being raised to $17,000.
ideas.startup_cost: $43,000 franchise cost; Alex says financed startup cash could be $5,000 to $10,000.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated; Alex says reaching average revenue takes a few years.

acquisition.how: The franchisor supplies leads and marketing tools, but channels and the human work needed to build trust are not specified.

onboarding.how: Training and licensing support are provided, but customer claim intake and case assessment likely need review.

delivery.how: Claims negotiation, judgement, and customer reassurance are human work; AI tools support the process.

billing.how: A percentage-based fee could be calculated from the claim, with human handling of minimums and the claim outcome.

support.how: Customers facing property damage need case-specific communication and claim support.

uk_applicability.notes: Property claims and claim advocacy exist in the UK, but the US franchise, licensing, insurer relationships, and SBA financing described would need substantial local adaptation.

risks: Insurance work is regulated and may require licences.

tactics.name: Match the franchise to the buyer
steps: Start by asking what the buyer wants from the business, their risk tolerance, operational background, and financial goals.
For risk-averse buyers, look for established brands with around 80 to 100 open units and 5 to 10 years or more of history.
For buyers seeking greater upside, consider earlier systems with protected territory while recognising that the risk is higher.

quote.text: I start with the individual like what do you want? What's your risk tolerance? What are you good at?
quote.speaker: Alex Smerzneck

tactics.name: Use franchise financing to reduce initial cash
steps: Ask lenders about SBA financing for the franchise.
Estimate the cash contribution after financing before committing.
Alex says friends or family may fund the remaining amount if the buyer lacks it.

quote.text: And if you don't have $10,000, you can get friends or family to finance that.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Check the franchise disclosure document and Item 19 footnotes
steps: Review the FDD for units sold and closed, closure reasons, lawsuits, litigation, and bankruptcies.
Read Item 19 financial disclosures and inspect footnotes for adjusted EBITDA or revenue.
Compare the stated earnings with franchisee costs and operating requirements before deciding.

quote.text: Look at the footnotes and make sure you're you're getting the whole whole set of information.
quote.speaker: Alex Smerzneck

tactics.name: Build a referral engine for home-sale preparation
steps: Use the franchisor's referral playbooks to approach real-estate agents and brokerages.
Build repeat relationships with agents who handle multiple home sales.
Create a dependable bench of electricians, plumbers, drywall workers, and other subcontractors.
Offer an option to pay at closing if the brand supports it.

quote.text: And if you get a high-volume realtor on your team, like that could be dozens of closings a year.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use routes and subscriptions for window-box services
steps: Sell installation per window as the initial project.
Offer different flower replacement frequencies and seasonal add-ons.
Schedule customers into regular routes to replace flowers and decorations.

quote.text: And then there's this recurring subscription, and they have, as you can imagine, all sorts of add-ons.
quote.speaker: Alex Smerzneck

tactics.name: Use franchise lead tools to find short-term rental cleaning clients
steps: Target Airbnb owners and operators as a cleaning niche.
Use franchise-provided lists and lead tools where available.
Contact prospects only through channels permitted by the applicable marketing and privacy rules.

quote.text: they have those tools to go scrape all the Airbnb owners and operators and, you know, drive you business.
quote.speaker: Alex Smerzneck

tactics.name: Scale a franchise portfolio around operating strengths
steps: Focus on raising or borrowing capital, selecting sites, opening locations, and operating teams.
Use the franchisor's systems for branding, supply chain, and menu innovation.
Repeat the process across additional units and, potentially, different brands.

quote.text: I go raise capital or I borrow capital and I repeat that.
quote.speaker: Alex Smerzneck

tactics.name: Use AI to review an FDD

Ask for red flags, yellow flags, and green flags.
Verify the resulting analysis against the source document and its footnotes.

warnings.warning: Alex says many brand-new franchise concepts fail; a founder who has franchised a business once is not proof that the system is durable.
Do not rely only on headline revenue or adjusted earnings. Alex says to inspect FDD footnotes and the full set of disclosures.
Home-improvement returns are based on estimates; the seller cannot know exactly what the house would have sold for without the work.
The flower-box service may be more exposed to a recession because it is a discretionary service for affluent households.
Franchise revenue and profit claims in the conversation are not independently verified here and may describe different operators or territories.
Cleaning lead generation based on scraped Airbnb-owner lists and cold outreach could raise privacy and marketing-law issues; UK electronic marketing rules must be followed.
The franchise model still requires an operator to manage people, physical work, sites, and service quality; it is not presented as unattended.

lessons.lesson: Choose a business that matches the buyer's risk tolerance, strengths, and financial objective rather than selecting solely by headline revenue.

evidence_quality.rationale: Alex describes first-hand experience building, scaling, and franchising businesses, but most featured franchise economics are third-party claims attributed to FDDs without the documents or operator-level detail in the transcript. Chris and Alex also use estimates and examples that are not independently verified here.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Alex promotes Franzy, his franchise-matching platform, including its AI matching and free coaching, while recommending franchise concepts.
